prerequisites.title: Paid Help Scout plan
prerequisites.detail: The Free plan has no API or integrations access. Standard allows up to 200 calls per minute without reporting endpoints, Plus 400 and Pro 800 with all endpoints.

prerequisites.title: Active invited Help Scout user
prerequisites.detail: Credentials must be tied to an active, invited user in the account, otherwise the API returns 401.

prerequisites.title: Possible admin or owner login
prerequisites.detail: Help Scout's Apps guide says to log in as an administrator or account owner to create an app. It is unclear whether this also applies to My apps.

steps.title: Create the OAuth2 app in Help Scout
steps.detail: Go to Your Profile > My apps and click Create My App. You will be asked for a redirection URL.
inputs: Help Scout login on a paid plan
steps.done_when: The app exists and shows an app ID and secret.

steps.title: Copy redirect URI from Composio
steps.detail: Take the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard and enter it as the app's redirection URL. It is required for the Authorization Code flow.
steps.done_when: The redirection URL in My apps matches Composio's.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the help_scout auth config through Composio's API using your own app ID as client ID and app secret as client secret.
steps.done_when: The auth config returns an ID.

steps.title: Connect a test account
steps.detail: Authorize through the Composio connect link with a user on a paid account, and confirm the connected account becomes active.
steps.done_when: The connected account shows active and an API call succeeds.

traps.title: Placeholder redirect URL only for Client Credentials
traps.detail: A placeholder redirect URL is accepted only if you use just the Client Credentials flow. Per-customer connections need a real redirection URL.

traps.title: Plan limits shape the agent
traps.detail: Rate limits are per plan, and Standard has no reporting endpoints. Check each customer's plan.

traps.title: Wrong app type
traps.detail: Help Scout has a separate Apps feature under Workspace > Apps with a callback URL. The Mailbox API OAuth app under My apps is what you need here.

blockers.what_it_means: The credentials are not tied to an active, invited user in the Help Scout account.
blockers.what_to_do: Use or invite an active user and reconnect.

evidence.question: G5
evidence.quote: Branding modifications are not permitted while verification is in progress.
evidence.answer: Branding cannot be changed while brand verification is in progress; verification must be cancelled first.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: The sensitive scope verification process typically takes 3-5 business days to complete.
evidence.answer: For Google APIs, the sensitive scope verification process typically takes 3 to 5 business days.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: The automated review usually completes in a few minutes.
evidence.answer: The automated brand verification review usually completes in a few minutes.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: Compliant verification results are valid for 7 days.
evidence.answer: Compliant brand verification results are valid for 7 days.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: If you don't publish within that timeframe, the status will change to Need to re-verify and you will have to run the brand verification again.
evidence.answer: If brand verification is not published within 7 days, it must be run again.

evidence.question: G6
evidence.quote: After you publish your branding or submit a data access request, Google's Trust & Safety team may follow up by email with any additional information they need or steps you must complete.
evidence.answer: After publishing branding or submitting a data access request, Google's Trust & Safety team may follow up by email with requests.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Sensitive scopes require review by Google before a Google Account can grant access and might be restricted by Google Workspace organization administrators.
evidence.answer: Google Workspace organization administrators can restrict sensitive scopes, and may do so with sensitive scope access.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: In this case, your app might need approval from an organization administrator.
evidence.answer: For internal apps, the app might need approval from an organization administrator.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: Organization administrators are the only accounts that can add the app to an allowlist for use within their domains.
evidence.answer: In a domain-wide installation, only organization administrators can add the app to an allowlist for their domains.

evidence.question: G8
evidence.quote: This is because a domain-wide installation lets a domain administrator grant third-party and internal applications access to your users' data.
evidence.answer: A domain-wide installation lets a domain administrator grant third-party and internal apps access to users' data.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Verify ownership of your project's authorized domains
evidence.answer: Ownership of the project's authorized domains must be verified, using Google Search Console.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Your home page must be publicly accessible, and not just accessible to your site's logged-in users.
evidence.answer: The app's home page must be publicly accessible, not only to logged-in users of the site.

evidence.question: G9
evidence.quote: Links to your app's listing on the Google Play Store or its Facebook page aren't considered valid application home pages.
evidence.answer: Links to a Google Play Store listing or a Facebook page are not valid application home pages.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Go to the Cloud Console OAuth Branding page
evidence.answer: Brand verification is started from the Cloud Console OAuth Branding page, where the developer selects the project.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: For example, a project can contain one or more OAuth clients, configure APIs for use by those clients, and configure an OAuth consent screen that's shown to users before they authorize access to your app.
evidence.answer: A Cloud Console project can contain one or more OAuth clients and an OAuth consent screen shown to users before they authorize the app.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: In the Branding page, provide your app's branding information, including app name, logo, developer contact information, and relevant links.
evidence.answer: On the Branding page, the developer enters app name, logo, developer contact information, and relevant links.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Click the Verify Branding button to start the evaluation process.
evidence.answer: The Verify Branding button starts the evaluation, and the Publish branding button makes the branding live.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Use the Add or remove scopes button to declare all scopes requested by your app.
evidence.answer: Scopes are declared with the Add or remove scopes button.

evidence.question: G10
evidence.quote: Note that you must have a published branding status before you can request verification for data access.
evidence.answer: Data-access verification requires a published branding status first, and is requested through the OAuth Verification Center.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: Preparation for verification includes checking exceptions, complying with branding, verifying domain ownership, and ensuring accurate OAuth consent screen information and policy links.
evidence.answer: Apps must comply with the branding requirements of the associated APIs or product and keep consent screen branding accurate.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: You must request the narrowest scope necessary for your app's functionality and ensure data usage complies with API policies and your privacy policy.
evidence.answer: Apps must use Google user data only in compliance with API policies and as disclosed in the privacy policy, and request the narrowest scope.

evidence.question: G11
evidence.quote: A user cap restricts the number of Google Accounts able to grant access to your unverified app.
evidence.answer: A user cap limits how many Google Accounts can use an unverified app.

Quote states the Free plan does not include API or integrations access.
Quote states each paid plan has different levels of API access.
Quote states up to 200 calls per minute; the plan attribution is implied by the quote's context in the statement but the quote itself is only the number and limit.
Quote says no access to reporting endpoints but does not explicitly tie it to the Standard plan in the quote itself.
Quote gives up to 400 calls per minute but does not show the Plus plan or that all endpoints are available.
Quote gives up to 800 calls per minute but does not show the Pro plan or that all endpoints are available.
Quote states that if only the Client Credentials flow is intended, a placeholder URL can be provided to continue generating the app.
Quote says Authorization Code is typically used for integrations used by other users, but does not state that no provider review is needed; it is silent on review.
Quote does not list the setup steps (create app under My apps, set redirect URL, connect via Authorization Code) or their order.
Quotes state the Free plan lacks API access and that each paid plan has different API access levels.
Quote states credentials must belong to an active, invited user, otherwise a 401 is returned.
Quote supports that Authorization Code is typical for cross-user integrations, but nothing supports the about-an-hour timing or the absence of a documented review.
